reasoning: The 10-K states the effective tax rate was *lower* than the statutory rate due to specific tax benefits. The 10-Q states the *decrease* in the effective tax rate was due to similar benefits relative to lower profitability. While both mention similar benefits, the 10-K doesn't explicitly link the lower rate to lower profitability, creating a narrative tension.
quoted_phrase_a: Our effective tax rate for fiscal year 2023 was lower than the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% due primarily to tax benefits from the FDII deduction, tax benefits related to stock-based compensation and the U.S. federal research tax credit.
quoted_phrase_b: The decrease in our effective tax rate for the third quarter and first nine months of fiscal year 2023 as compared to the same periods of fiscal year 2022 was primarily due to the increased tax benefit of the foreign-derived intangible income deduction, stock-based compensation, and the U.S. federal research tax credit, relative to a lower expected profitability.
